claims.answer: Tauri desktop app for Windows x64, macOS (universal, Apple silicon, Intel) and Linux (AppImage/deb/rpm), a web app served by a local or remote Helicon server, and a VS Code extension; no phone app (mobile relay is an unchecked roadmap item).

desktop_os.answer: v0.23.4 assets: Helicon_0.23.4_x64-setup.exe, universal/aarch64/x64 DMGs, amd64 AppImage, deb and rpm; minimum OS versions not stated.

mobile_apps.answer: No mobile app; "Post-v1: mobile relay" is unchecked in the README roadmap.

browser.answer: Web app (`npm run serve --workspace @helicon/web`) and hosted demo; remote daemon mode via #/connect.

mobile_browser.answer: The web UI is a browser page and could be opened from a phone against a remote daemon; no mobile-specific layout or support is documented.

cli.answer: `@helicon/server` CLI (node packages/server/dist/src/cli.js with --host/--token/--port) starts the server; it does not run chats.

editor_extensions.answer: VS Code extension (Marketplace and Open VSX for Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity); helicon.vsix in the release.

task_actions.answer: Start threads, send/queue follow-ups, resume, approve or reject actions, stop turns and monitors, steer goals, open files.

notifications.answer: OS notifications in the Tauri desktop shell and browser Notifications API in the web app for approval requests, questions, finished or failed turns and goal changes; user switch in Settings, suppressed while the window is focused; no mobile push.

cross_device_continuity.answer: A remote daemon with token lets another browser attach; state is local SQLite on the daemon host.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: mobile_apps, mobile_browser, cli, notifications, cross_device_continuity; see atomic answers.

claims.answer: Code, prompts and threads stay local and go to Muse/Meta under the user plan; Helicon stores no credentials of its own and keeps its state in a local SQLite file. Installed v0.23.4 builds have no analytics, but the desktop update check, which runs by default, sends platform, version and a weekly-salted IP hash that the vendor uses to count installs; Settings > Pause updates stops the scheduled checks.

code_data.answer: Stays local; Muse sends to Meta per its terms.

prompts.answer: Same; Contributor-tier prompts may be used by Meta.

credentials.answer: Helicon stores no credentials of its own: Muse logins stay with the muse CLI (~/.config/muse/auth.json), and named profiles are managed by aonia. In remote-daemon mode the web app keeps the daemon address and token in browser local storage and exchanges the token for an HttpOnly cookie.

deletion.answer: No in-app erase: removing a project only hides it (DELETE /api/projects sets hidden). Users delete Helicon's local state by removing ~/.helicon/helicon.db (or run with --data-dir :memory:); thread transcripts belong to the muse CLI.

training.answer: README flags Contributor-tier training use by Meta.

subprocessors.answer: The desktop update check goes to helicon.sh with a GitHub fallback; model traffic goes to Muse/Meta under the user's plan. No processor list is published.

telemetry_defaults.answer: On by default (desktop): installed v0.23.4 builds have no analytics, but the desktop app checks for updates 5 seconds after launch and every six hours with Pause updates off by default, and the README says that check sends platform, version and a weekly-salted IP hash that the vendor uses to count installs in use.

telemetry_controls.answer: Pause updates toggle stops scheduled checks; no telemetry-labelled control.

telemetry_off_switch.answer: In the app: at v0.23.4 the Settings "Pause updates" toggle stops the scheduled install-counting update checks (launch and every six hours). Only a check the user deliberately starts still contacts helicon.sh, which is a one-off action rather than ongoing telemetry. There is no telemetry-labelled switch.

consent_prompt.answer: None: at v0.23.4 the desktop app starts its update checks 5 seconds after launch with Pause updates off by default, with no prompt or consent step in the update controller.

evidence.finding: 114 stars, MIT, homepage helicon.sh, TypeScript, pushed 2026-11-16.

evidence.title: Release v0.23.4 assets
evidence.finding: Latest release 2026-11-16 with Windows x64 setup exe, universal/arm64/x64 macOS DMGs, Linux AppImage, deb and rpm, helicon.vsix, signatures and latest.json.

evidence.title: README
evidence.locator: intro; Idea; Architecture; Roadmap; Install; Remote daemon; What leaves your machine; Legal
evidence.finding: Free MIT desktop app and VS Code extension for Meta Muse Code CLI; projects, sessions, approvals, goals, monitors, file viewer, plan meter, WSL routing, remote daemon, SQLite state; no account or analytics, update check only; unofficial.

evidence.title: CHANGELOG
evidence.finding: Recent shipped changes: DMG per Mac chip, VS Code image paste, Computer Use approvals naming sent data, WSL distro fix, SDK 1.4.20, long-thread freeze fix.

evidence.title: VS Code extension README
evidence.locator: What you get; How it works
evidence.finding: Side panel for the open folder with threads as tabs, history, readable approvals, inline diffs, plan usage and cost, several Muse accounts, SSH projects, monitors; local server bound to 127.0.0.1.

evidence.title: MSP host
evidence.finding: Daemon spawns `muse serve` and speaks Muse Session Protocol through the official SDK; no TUI scraping.

evidence.title: Local store
evidence.finding: SQLite via node:sqlite: projects with pins, hidden, default account; sessions with title source ranking.

evidence.title: SSH projects
evidence.finding: Projects at ssh://host/path run Muse on the remote host over a passwordless non-interactive ssh stdio connection with keepalives.

evidence.title: WSL routing
evidence.finding: Windows routes Muse natively or into WSL2 with path translation and a selectable distro.

evidence.title: Server CLI flags
evidence.finding: Server binds 127.0.0.1 by default; --host, --token and repeatable --allow-origin enable remote daemon mode.

evidence.title: Server
evidence.finding: Server aggregates subscription usage windows, thread discovery, titles and host commands.

evidence.title: Approval policy parsing
evidence.finding: Approval modes Ask first/Full access map to MSP policies onRequest/allowAll etc.

evidence.title: Monitors panel
evidence.finding: Thread shows background monitors with elapsed time and a Stop button.

evidence.title: Workflow model
evidence.finding: UI models Muse workflow runs with agents that can be cancelled, skipped or retried.

evidence.title: Usage import
evidence.finding: Usage store records token calls priced at API rates; also imports oh-my-pi muse-code sessions.

evidence.title: Security policy
evidence.finding: Pre-release; private advisory reporting; 72-hour acknowledgement target.

evidence.title: LICENSE
evidence.finding: MIT License © 2026 Harjot Singh Rana and contributors.

evidence.title: Demo animation (demo.gif)
evidence.finding: Real Helicon window mid-run: project list, thread brisk-photon Working 18s, inline diff, failed and passing test runs, composer.

evidence.title: helicon.sh home
evidence.finding: Vendor site with downloads, pricing page (free and MIT), changelog and machine-readable facts.

evidence.title: Bounded search: accounts, SSO, roles
evidence.finding: No accounts, roles or SSO; remote daemon uses a single token.

evidence.title: Bounded search: schedules and webhooks
evidence.finding: No Helicon scheduler or webhook endpoints; matches are UI strings for Muse features.

evidence.title: Bounded search: Git/PR/trackers
evidence.locator: grep createPullRequest|gh pr|git commit|worktree add|linear|jira over packages/ apps/
evidence.finding: No Git commit, PR or worktree-creation code and no tracker integration; PR watching is done by the Muse agent through monitors.

evidence.title: Bounded search: vendor cloud and isolation
evidence.locator: grep docker|container|sandbox|vendor cloud over packages/ apps/
evidence.finding: No vendor runtime or container/VM isolation; matches are WSL and SSH routing code.

evidence.title: Bounded search: other harnesses
evidence.finding: Only the Muse Code MSP backend is implemented; ACP appears only in docs comparing other editors.

evidence.title: Bounded search: telemetry and analytics
evidence.finding: Installed builds have no analytics; apps/web/src/demo/tryAnalytics.ts sends page analytics to PostHog only in the hosted helicon.sh/try demo build (VITE_TRY), and the update check goes to helicon.sh with GitHub fallback.

evidence.title: Notification model
evidence.finding: The UI raises notifications for an approval request, a question, a finished or failed turn and a goal status change, with a user on/off switch, suppression while the window is focused and a 20 second repeat guard.

evidence.title: Notifier implementations
evidence.finding: The browser build uses the Notifications API and the desktop shell uses Tauri's OS notification plugin; the settings page has a notifications toggle.

evidence.title: Helicon README "What leaves your machine"
evidence.finding: The desktop update check to helicon.sh sends platform, version and a weekly-salted IP hash and is used to count installs in use; the README states there are no analytics in the app.

evidence.title: Helicon update controller and Settings updates rows
evidence.locator: updates.ts check(): scheduled checks skip while paused; SettingsPage.tsx "Pause updates" toggle
evidence.finding: Scheduled update checks are skipped while the Settings "Pause updates" toggle is on; a manual check still contacts the server.

evidence.title: Helicon README at v0.23.4: What leaves your machine
evidence.finding: The README says there is no account and no analytics in the app; the desktop update check to helicon.sh sends the platform, the version and a weekly-salted IP hash and is how the vendor counts roughly how many installs are in use.

evidence.title: Helicon v0.23.4 update controller and Settings page
evidence.locator: packages/ui/src/model/updates.ts lines 101-108 (check(): scheduled checks return while paused, manual checks proceed); packages/ui/src/components/settings/SettingsPage.tsx lines 668-669 (Pause updates toggle)
evidence.finding: At tag v0.23.4 the Settings page has a Pause updates toggle described as 'No checking, downloading or installing until you resume'. The update controller skips scheduled checks while paused; a check the user asks for directly still contacts the update server.

evidence.title: Helicon update scheduling at v0.23.4
evidence.locator: packages/ui/src/model/updates.ts lines 47-48 (FIRST_CHECK_MS 5s, RECHECK_MS 6h), 79-90 (start schedules checks), 101-108 (paused skips scheduled checks); packages/ui/src/model/controller.ts lines 352-353 and 387-389; packages/ui/src/model/store.ts line 171 (updatesPaused: false)
evidence.finding: When the desktop app starts, the controller starts the UpdateManager, which schedules an update check 5 seconds after launch and every six hours. updatesPaused defaults to false, so these checks run without any user action; there is no prompt or consent step before them. With Pause updates on, scheduled checks return early; only a check the user explicitly asks for (manual) still contacts the update server.

evidence.title: Helicon README: Architecture, Install, local state and Remote daemon
evidence.locator: README.md line 97 (Auth), lines 119-127 (Install), line 166 (state in ~/.helicon/helicon.db), lines 193-207 (Remote daemon); docs/CHANGELOG.md line 295 (Accounts via aonia)
evidence.finding: Helicon uses the user's own muse login (~/.config/muse/auth.json) and never stores credentials of its own; named Muse profiles are managed by aonia, so the CLI owns every login. When the web app connects to a remote daemon, the daemon address and token are kept in browser local storage, and the token is exchanged once for an HttpOnly cookie used by the event stream. Projects, pins, thread titles and archive state persist in ~/.helicon/helicon.db (movable with --data-dir, or :memory: for a throwaway run).

evidence.title: Helicon server DELETE /api/projects
evidence.locator: packages/server/src/server.ts lines 1239-1247; search of packages/server/src for DELETE handlers
evidence.finding: Removing a project calls store.setHidden(cwd, true): the project is hidden, not erased. The only other DELETE handler removes a named Muse profile through aonia. The server has no route that erases stored threads or the local database.
